title: [DualTor][QoS Remapping] The test case test_pfc_pause_extra_lossless_standby could fail if we run the dualtor topology on a platform who has more than 32 ports

**Description**
The test case test_pfc_pause_extra_lossless_standby could fail if we run the dualtor topology on a platform who has more than 32 ports.

Why this could happen:

- The test firstly sends a packet to one of the uplink port and finds the actual egress port of the bounced back packet. After it gets the number of the receiving ptf port, it uses the number to find the corresponding interface on the dut by searching the ptf port number in mg_facts['minigraph_ptf_indices'].

- If the actual egress port is Ethernet120 for example(it's determined by the ecmp), the ptf port number is 32 in dualtor topology on the upper tor(for example, the dut is randomly selected in the test).

- And the mg_facts['minigraph_ptf_indices'] is like this:

[(u'Ethernet8', 2), (u'Ethernet0', 0), (u'Ethernet4', 1), (u'Ethernet248', 62), (u'Ethernet244', 61), **(u'Ethernet128', 32)**, (u'Ethernet240', 60), (u'Ethernet40', 10), (u'Ethernet200', 50), (u'Ethernet124', 34), (u'Ethernet204', 51), **(u'Ethernet120', 32),** (u'Ethernet208', 52), (u'Ethernet160', 40), (u'Ethernet164', 41), (u'Ethernet76', 19), (u'Ethernet72', 18), (u'Ethernet32', 8), (u'Ethernet36', 9), (u'Ethernet136', 34), (u'Ethernet132', 33), (u'Ethernet232', 58), (u'Ethernet172', 43), (u'Ethernet236', 59), (u'Ethernet176', 44), (u'Ethernet64', 16), (u'Ethernet60', 15), (u'Ethernet20', 5), (u'Ethernet24', 6), (u'Ethernet180', 45), (u'Ethernet44', 11), (u'Ethernet184', 46), (u'Ethernet188', 47), (u'Ethernet108', 27), (u'Ethernet100', 25), (u'Ethernet212', 53), (u'Ethernet104', 26), (u'Ethernet228', 57), (u'Ethernet96', 24), (u'Ethernet148', 37), (u'Ethernet92', 23), (u'Ethernet28', 7), (u'Ethernet220', 55), (u'Ethernet144', 36), (u'Ethernet52', 13), (u'Ethernet224', 56), (u'Ethernet140', 35), (u'Ethernet56', 14), (u'Ethernet16', 4), (u'Ethernet12', 3), (u'Ethernet196', 49), (u'Ethernet192', 48), (u'Ethernet168', 42), (u'Ethernet116', 30), (u'Ethernet80', 20), (u'Ethernet112', 28), (u'Ethernet84', 21), (u'Ethernet152', 38), (u'Ethernet156', 39), (u'Ethernet48', 12), (u'Ethernet216', 54), (u'Ethernet68', 17), (u'Ethernet88', 22), (u'Ethernet252', 63)]


- We can see the ptf port number of Ethernet128 is also 32 , and because Ethernet128 is in front of Ethernet120 in the list, the test wil consider Ethernet128 as the actual egress port and send pfc storm to it, which will cause the test to fail.

The root cause is we replace the ptf ports number of the uplink ports for the dualtor topology. And if we have more ports in the platform than defined in the topology, we will face this issue.

**Steps to reproduce the issue:**
1. Deploy the dualtor topology on a platform who has more than 32 physical ports(such as Mellanox 4600C)
2. Run the test case tests/qos/test_tunnel_qos_remap.py::test_pfc_pause_extra_lossless_standby
3. There is a chance to see this issue if meets the conditions in the description.

**Describe the results you received:**
In the test log:

comments.author: congh-nvidia
comments.body: Hi @rbpittman, this issue is about the new qos remapping test case you added in PR (https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/pull/9318), and I have made a draft fix in (https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/pull/10140), could you please check and review? If you are OK with the fix, I will upstream it. Thanks.

comments.author: rbpittman
comments.body:
Hi @congh-nvidia, thanks for filing the issue. I've also run into this, but figured it was an anomaly in our test setups, good to see it's common across platforms. 

I was wondering what caused the port_name->ptf_index map to have multiple port_name's that map to the same ptf_index. Discovered there's a place where the mapping is constructed as the composition of two maps, but is initialized as well, causing duplicates to occur. 

Filed #10144 to see if you have any thoughts. This fixed the issue for me locally, but I was concerned about how this could affect other platforms given odd usage of try-excepts in the surrounding code.

comments.author: congh-nvidia
comments.body: Hi @rbpittman , your fix looks good to me, the test passed on our testbed with it. Thanks!

comments.author: rbpittman
comments.body: Thanks for verifying! Requesting review or assignee from @bingwang-ms on the PR.

comments.author: bingwang-ms
comments.body:
Thanks @congh-nvidia @rbpittman catching this issue. It's a great catch.
Change in https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/pull/10144 makes sense to me. The map `mg_facts['minigraph_port_indices']`  contains all front panel ports, including both admin up and admin down ports. However, only the ptf index of ports in `tbinfo['topo']['ptf_map'][str(dut_index)]` are updated into map `mg_facts['minigraph_ptf_indices']`. That may cause ptf index conflict. 
My concern for this change is, the admin down ports will be removed from map `mg_facts['minigraph_ptf_indices']`. I'm not 100% sure if we have any test case that queries the index for admin down ports (probably not). 
Since it's a pretty fundamental change, I suggest @wangxin help review this change.
Another work around is, we add the disabled port into `host_interfaces` section as well in the topo definition file. All port index in the map `mg_facts['minigraph_ptf_indices']` will also be updated in this way.
Please let me know if I miss anything. Thanks!

comments.author: rbpittman
comments.body:
As I understand your latter suggestion, it'd involve the same change but with extra entries in the ptf_map so all mappings can be both present and unique. Not sure how/where this would be added.

Regardless, it might be good to just not have any down ports if they're not needed. 

cc @wangxin for assistance

### Description of PR
<!--
- Please include a summary of the change and which issue is fixed.
- Please also include relevant motivation and context. Where should reviewer start? background context?
- List any dependencies that are required for this change.
-->

The `minigraph_ptf_indices` structure maps port names to PTF indices. From the code context, it appears that `minigraph_port_indices` was used for this mapping, but multi-dut TBs caused problems with the PTF.

It seems the more reliable way to get the ptf indices is to compose together the port_name->port_index map (`minigraph_port_indices`), and the port_index->ptf_index map (`tbinfo['topo']['ptf_map'][str(dut_index)]`). 

The pre-existing initialization of this composition to include any members of the `port_index->ptf_index` map can leave duplicate ptf_index entries for down ports, especially in dualtor scenarios. See #10139. 

Remove the extra initialization on the composition construction.
